sfx_review.label: impact
sfx_review.note: Low-frequency boom with sustained bass tail starting ~20.30 s, not the tonal partials of a chime; lands mid-turn of the phone, could also be a music bass hit.

pattern.description: While the Gemini answer is still loading (gradient shimmer travelling along placeholder bars), the whole phone yaws in 3D so its glowing side rail swings into view and the screen content shifts right in perspective, with a slight scale-down.
pattern.why_premium: Turning the hardware during the wait converts dead loading time into a product beauty shot; the rim light on the rail and the continuous shimmer keep both device and software alive in the same move.

build_hint.gsap: Wrap the screen UI in a .device with transformPerspective:1200; gsap.fromTo('.device', {rotationY:0, scale:1}, {rotationY:-18, scale:0.93, duration:0.6, ease:'power2.inOut'}); shimmer runs independently: gsap.fromTo('.bar', {backgroundPosition:'-100% 0'}, {backgroundPosition:'200% 0', duration:1.2, ease:'none', repeat:-1, stagger:0.15}). Screen children inherit the transform (no separate tweens).
build_hint.remotion: const t = interpolate(frame, [0, 14], [0, 1], {easing: Easing.inOut(Easing.quad), extrapolateRight:'clamp'}); style={{transform:`perspective(1200px) rotateY(${-18*t}deg) scale(${1-0.07*t})`}}; bar gradient offset = (frame % 36) / 36 for a looping linear shimmer.

notes: camera.move is none; scale 0.93 reflects the device turning/receding, not a camera pull-out (it could also be a real camera orbit around a physical render, which the frame alone cannot distinguish). Screen elements move only as part of the phone, not independently. Disclaimer line b07 is barely changed and omitted.
